 now 03.37 EST Like a US midterm electoral map it is a sea of blue inside Allianz Stadium this evening. It is a sellout and the vast majority of fans are here to cheer on Samoa, not the nominal home team, Australia.
 Share 4m ago 03.32 EST Team News
 Australia : Kevin Walters revealed his hand last weekend so it is no surprise to see Reece Walsh starting ahead of James Tedesco at fullback, and Tom Dearden beating Sam Walker in the race for a starting berth in the halves. Latrell Mitchell and Cameron Murray are fit enough to make the bench, where they will join Ethan Strange, who retains his place after an eye-catching cameo against Cook Islands.
 Samoa: Just one enforced change for Ben Gardiner with Ronald Volkman replacing the injured Chanel Harris-Tavita at five-eighth. The Eel came on for the Warrior against Tonga after the starting No 6 pulled his hamstring kicking for goal.

 Jonathan Howcroft Hello everybody and welcome to live coverage of Australia v Samoa in the second semi-final of the 2026 men’s Rugby League World Cup . Kick-off at Allianz Stadium in Sydney is from 8.05pm local time (9.05am GMT). 
 The penultimate fixture of a thoroughly entertaining tournament will determine who will start the 2026 men’s rugby league world cup final against New Zealand as underdogs. It would be among the greatest upsets in the sport’s history if Australia are not on the bill to face the Kiwis in Brisbane next weekend but the Kangaroos have yet to hit any kind of form and they will be facing a fiercely motivated foe in Samoa.
 Rugby League World Cup: adversaries gather at Australia’s gate but main threat comes from within | Jack Snape Read more To say Australia’s world cup so far has been underwhelming but would be an understatement. Kevin Walters’ squad and team selection has invited criticism, his forward pack has been well beaten twice, and matches have been won by moments of individual brilliance as opposed to methodical representative football. If the strategy has to been to ease into the contest after a gruelling NRL season then tonight is when the shackles have to be removed.
 Tonga’s gripping win over Samoa a victory for Pasifika pride at Rugby League World Cup Read more Samoa boast a side studded with State of Origin matchwinners, many of whom would command places in the current Australian line-up. And they will have a point to prove after falling narrowly to Tonga last time out in a match where they had enough chances to win.
 They have the power up front to rattle Australia, and the strike out wide to finish them off. The challenge will be whether the spine can control proceedings when the stakes are so high.
 I’ll be back with final team lists and more shortly. Please send me your emails and keep me company throughout the evening. The address is jonathan.howcroft.freelance@theguardian.com .
